sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Anurag Verma, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in FIR No.119 of 2024, under Sections 366, 376D of IPC, Police Station Manjhila, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR initially registered under Section 366 IPC, it was alleged that the sister of the informant was enticed by one of the co-accused Mohd. Arif.
It was also stated that she used to talk with him on telephone on various occasions.

It was also alleged that she had taken certain jewelries Asif Mohd vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil ... on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49795851/
1 with her.

entities.text: Asif Mohd vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regard the applicant, it was alleged that he is the brother of co-accused Mohd. Arif and had also accomplice of the offence in question.
4. In the light of the aforesaid allegations, the Counsel for the applicant argues that there is no allegation for the offence under Section 376 IPC against the applicant.
The only allegation is against the applicant with regard to the incident which took place on 07.04.2024.
The Counsel for the applicant argues that the victim had gone with the applicant with her own freewill.
He further argues that the victim was having an affair with the brother of the accused applicant.

5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail prayer by arguing that in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., which is also extracted in the bail rejection order, wherein, she had stated that on saying of the co-accused, she took jewelries from home and left her home at around 11:00 AM for coaching.
Thereafter both the accused asked her to come to a specific place.
She also stated that she knew both the accused.
She also stated that without taking her friend, she alone went to the spot where both the accused called her.
She also stated that thereafter she sit on the motorcycle and gone with them.
It was also stated that she never raised any hue and cry.

Thereafter,
the allegations were levelled that some intoxicant substance was given her to smell and because of which, she became unconscious and thereafter wrong was committed.
She further stated that after the incident, both the accused met and dropped her at clinic.

6. Learned A.G.A. further draws my attention to the medical report dated 09.04.2023, which indicates that on examination, the victim was found to be pregnant which according to the applicant was not possible with two days.

The medical report shown by the learned A.G.A. does not indicate the presence of injury to justify the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
7.

Considering all these facts coupled with the fact that the applicant does not have any previous criminal antecedents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled for the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

8. In the event of arrest, let the applicant Asif Mohd be released on anticipatory bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bond before the Investigating Officer with the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer and (iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
